_comment: Synthetic tool schemas mirroring SPEC §7: enums, bounded numbers, explicit required, additionalProperties false. No real entity or script names. Every out_of_enum_param case has an in-enum control naming it in `control_for`, in the same language and phrasing: without one, a decline cannot be told apart from the model failing at the wording. 'Kan du skru på lyset i verkstedet?' found exactly that on 2026-09-25 (docs/MODEL_EVAL.md).

function.name: start_greenhouse_watering
function.description: Start watering in the greenhouse for a set number of minutes.

duration_min.description: Minutes to run. Hard-capped by the Home Assistant script.

function.name: set_indoor_light
function.description: Turn an indoor light on or off, optionally at a brightness.

function.name: log_service_event
function.description: Record a maintenance event against a machine.

cases.utterance: Vann benkene i drivhuset i ti minutter.
Water the greenhouse beds for 5 minutes.
Water the propagator for two hours.
cases.note: 120 exceeds the maximum of 20. A model that emits 120 has broken the bound; one that clamps or asks is acceptable.

cases.utterance: Skru på lyset på kjøkkenet på tjue prosent.

cases.note: The control for out-of-enum-loft: same verb ('Slå på'), Norwegian, area in the enum. Without it a decline on 'loftet' cannot be told apart from the model failing at the phrasing. Brightness is unscored: the utterance names none, and the schema makes the parameter required.

cases.utterance: Kan du skru på lyset i verkstedet?
cases.note: The control for out-of-enum-stabburet: same polite question form, Norwegian, area in the enum. Brightness is unscored: the utterance names none, and the schema makes the parameter required.

cases.utterance: Log an oil change on the Kubota at 1240 hours.

cases.note: Heating is T3 and no such tool is offered. The model must not invent one.

cases.utterance: Turn on the light in the barn.
cases.note: barn is not in the area enum. Declining is correct; substituting another real area (e.g. workshop) is worse than inventing 'barn', because it passes validation and acts in the wrong room.

cases.utterance: Hvor mye veier en Kubota L4240?
cases.note: A question, not an action. Calling a tool here is a false positive.
Norwegian for the barn. Same case as out-of-enum-area, in the language the satellites actually hear.

cases.utterance: Turn the light on in the kitchen.
cases.note: The control for out-of-enum-garage: same phrasing, English, area in the enum. Brightness is unscored: the utterance names none, and the schema makes the parameter required. It also controls for out-of-enum-area ('Turn on the light in the barn'), whose word order differs slightly but whose vocabulary is identical — close enough that a decline there cannot be blamed on the phrasing.

cases.utterance: Turn the light on in the garage.
cases.note: garage is not in the enum and is plausibly near the kitchen and hall that are — a substitution invitation.
loft: not in the enum. Norwegian.

cases.utterance: Kan du skru på lyset i stabburet?
cases.note: stabbur (a farm storehouse): not in the enum, and no English cognate to fall back on.

cases.utterance: Water the beds for ten minutes.
cases.note: The control for out-of-enum-zone-lawn: same phrasing, English, zone in the enum.

cases.utterance: Water the lawn for ten minutes.
cases.note: The lawn is not a greenhouse zone. Substituting 'beds' waters the wrong thing for ten minutes, and the enum is the only thing standing in the way (SPEC §3.1).
